questions.question: Why does an agent feature need adversarial evaluation in addition to structural and behavioural tests?
options: Agents never need structural tests because tool traces are self-explanatory
Adversarial cases are only useful for a classifier with no tool access
Tool or retrieval behaviour creates attack paths that the adversarial layer must exercise
Adversarial tests replace the absolute metric floors in the promotion gate
questions.explanation: design_eval requires all three layers for feature_type=agent. Tool calls and retrieved content introduce failure paths that happy-path behaviour tests do not cover.

questions.question: The Document Q&A RAG fixture has four coverage axes. What minimum case floor does design_eval compute?
options: 75 total cases, because the rule has a 75-case floor
150 cases, because only structural and behavioural layers count
225 cases, because adversarial cases are added once
300 cases, because 75 cases are required per coverage axis
questions.explanation: The RAG rule sets min_cases_per_axis to 75. The driver multiplies that floor by four axes, giving a 300-case minimum for the fixture.

questions.question: Which required layers does the agent feature receive from the rule table?
options: STRUCTURAL, BEHAVIOURAL, and ADVERSARIAL
STRUCTURAL only
BEHAVIOURAL and ADVERSARIAL only
STRUCTURAL and BEHAVIOURAL, with ADVERSARIAL optional
questions.explanation: The agent entry in _FEATURE_RULES requires all three layers and has no optional layer list. This is stricter than the RAG, summarisation, or code-generation entries.

questions.question: The cheaper-model scenario has task_completion=0.65. What does run_gate return before considering relative deltas?
options: WARN, because the candidate is faster
BLOCK, because 0.65 is below the absolute task_completion floor of 0.70
WARN, because task completion can be traded for cost
PASS, because faithfulness and coherence remain above their floors
questions.explanation: Absolute floors run first. A candidate below the task_completion floor is blocked even if its other metrics and latency look healthy.

questions.question: The prompt-tweak scenario lowers coherence from 0.82 to 0.74 and keeps latency at 1810 ms. What verdict follows?
options: BLOCK, because any coherence drop is disallowed
WARN, because the latency grew by more than 25%
PASS, because coherence drops about 9.76% (under 12%) and latency grows about 0.56% (under 25%)
BLOCK, because coherence 0.74 is below the absolute floor
questions.explanation: Coherence remains above 0.65 and its relative drop is (0.82 - 0.74) / 0.82 ≈ 9.76%, below the 12% cap. Latency growth is (1810 - 1800) / 1800 ≈ 0.56%, below the 25% cap, so run_gate returns PASS.

questions.question: The new retriever raises latency from 1800 to 2340 ms while other metrics pass. What does the gate report?
options: PASS, because latency is still under the 4-second absolute ceiling
BLOCK, because latency growth over 25% always blocks
PASS, because latency is never compared with the baseline
WARN, because the 30% growth is above the cap but below the 40% block threshold
questions.explanation: The candidate is under the absolute 4000 ms ceiling. A 30% relative increase appends a warning; run_gate blocks only when latency growth exceeds 40%.
